title: Salesforce is putting Claude at the centre of its products, and itself inside Claude
excerpt: Salesforce and Anthropic have announced Claudeforce, making Claude the default model across Agentforce and Slack and Salesforce a plugin inside Claude.
content_html:
Salesforce and Anthropic have announced an expanded partnership called Claudeforce, which puts Claude at the centre of Salesforce’s agent products and simultaneously puts Salesforce inside Claude as a plugin.

It formalises a relationship that already runs deep enough that Salesforce expects to spend around $300mn on Anthropic tokens this year, and it comes on top of a stake in Anthropic now valued at about $5bn.

The first half is the conventional one. Claude is now the reasoning model behind Salesforce’s Atlas Reasoning Engine, powers Agentforce Vibes and Agentforce Coworker by default, and is available in Agent Builder, all of which are live today.

For regulated industries, there is a specific deployment path that matters more than it sounds. Claude can be accessed through Amazon Bedrock inside what Salesforce calls its Trust Boundary, which is the arrangement banks and healthcare customers need before they will let a model near their records.

Salesforce is not the first large vendor to make Claude a default. What stands out here is the breadth, covering the reasoning engine, the agent builder, and the messaging product in one go.

Slack gets the same treatment. Claude becomes the default model there too, powering Slackbot, the Claude Tag, and Slack Code, which Salesforce describes as bridging team conversation with autonomous action.

The company offers one number for how that is going internally. Slackbot has produced 8.1 million annualised hours of productivity at Salesforce itself, a figure it says has doubled quarter on quarter.

The second half of the announcement is the more interesting one, and it runs the other way. Salesforce is shipping a plugin called Salesforce in Claude, giving sellers 37 prebuilt sales skills that work inside Anthropic’s own interface rather than inside Salesforce’s.

The skills cover the recognisable parts of a sales week: meeting preparation, deal health review, and pipeline review, with the ability to update pipelines and execute what Salesforce calls governed actions.

Onboarding reads across Salesforce, Slack, and connected systems to generate a tailored dashboard, and administrators connect it once with central authentication and permissions.

The governance language is doing real work in that description. An agent that can read a pipeline is a demo, whereas one that can update it needs permissions, an audit trail, and an administrator able to revoke it, which is the part enterprise buyers have been waiting on.

It is worth pausing on what that arrangement means commercially. Salesforce has spent twenty-five years insisting that its interface is where enterprise work happens, and it has just agreed to become a component inside somebody else’s.

That is not obviously a concession, because the alternative is being routed around entirely. If sellers are going to start the day in a chat interface anyway, appearing there with governed write access beats being the system they alt-tab to afterwards.

“By fusing Claude’s extraordinary reasoning with the trusted data, workflows, and governance every enterprise runs on, we’re delivering a dynamic interface that thinks, reasons, and acts,” said Marc Benioff, Salesforce’s chair and chief executive.

Dario Amodei, Anthropic’s chief executive and co-founder, framed it from the data side. “Through this partnership, companies can point Claude at customer information and business context they’ve been building in Salesforce for decades, and use it to actually run and grow their businesses,” he said.

For Anthropic, the appeal is distribution, plainly. Salesforce and Slack, between them, sit inside a very large share of enterprise sales and support work, which is a substantial amount of daily usage to acquire through a single agreement.

On timing, Salesforce and Claude are in pilot now with an open beta due in September, and further prebuilt skills are promised for late 2026. No pricing was disclosed for any part of the announcement.

The unresolved question is one Salesforce staff have already been asking about the Claude Tag in Slack. Making a supplier’s model the default across your product line, and your product a feature of theirs, is a deep bet on that supplier remaining a partner.
